title: Agent permission manifest
description: The default-deny side of the action scope validator, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #70: named agents pinned to rungs of the autonomy ladder, each granted only actions the registry declares and each argument constrained by a scope pattern. Nothing on this page is authority — it is a claim, judged against the registry. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/actions); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — agent names unique, grants per agent unique, granted actions actually declared in the registry (a grant for an undeclared action is a phantom), argument scopes naming parameters the granted action actually declares, stages that do not contradict the granted effects (a read-only agent may hold no write), a quarantined agent holding no grants at all, and reviews not older than 365 days nor in the future.

owner.description: Who owns the manifest and answers for what the agents may do. Permissions nobody owns are nobody's permissions.

reviewedOn.description: Date the manifest was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

agents.description: The agents and what they are allowed to do. Absent from this page means denied — the manifest is a claim, not a constitution.

agent.description: The agent's name. Unique across the manifest.

stage.description: The agent's rung on the autonomy ladder. Closed vocabulary. A read-only agent granted a write, or a quarantined agent granted anything, contradicts its stage.

grants.description: The actions this agent may perform. Each names a registry-declared action and constrains its arguments with scope patterns.

action.description: The granted action id. Must be declared in the action registry — a grant for an undeclared action is a hope wearing a permission's clothes.

argumentScopes.description: The argument scoping for the granted action. Each scope names a parameter the action declares and a pattern the runtime must check the value against.

parameter.description: The parameter this scope constrains. Must be declared by the granted action.

pattern.description: The glob pattern the argument value must match at call time — e.g. 'INV-2026-*'. An unscoped argument is unscoped authority.
